nodes.description: bytes32 public state variable storing keccak256 hash of the correct answer string; gates the Try() payout and is rewritten by set_game() and NewQuestion().
Public string state variable holding the current question text; written by set_game() and NewQuestion().

Address state variable acting as owner/administrator; set to msg.sender in set_game() and reassigned by newQuestioner(). Used as the access-control guard in StopGame(), NewQuestion() and newQuestioner().
External payable function that requires msg.sender == tx.origin, verifies keccak256(_response) == responseHash and msg.value > 3 ether, then transfers the whole contract balance to msg.sender.
Public payable initializer: if responseHash is still zero it stores keccak256(_response), the question text and makes msg.sender the questionSender.
Public payable function that requires msg.sender == questionSender and transfers the entire contract balance to the caller; external ETH transfer to an arbitrary owner address.
Public payable function allowing questionSender to replace the question and the answer hash.
Public function allowing the current questionSender to hand ownership over to a newAddress.
Payable fallback function with empty body; executes when ETH is sent to the contract without matching calldata.
Attacker-controllable caller address; used as ownership claimant, access-control subject and ETH transfer recipient.
Transaction origin address used in the require(msg.sender == tx.origin) check inside Try(), restricting the payout path to externally owned accounts.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside Try(): external ETH transfer of the full contract balance to an attacker-supplied address.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside StopGame(): external ETH transfer of the full contract balance to the owner address.
String parameter _response of Try(), hashed and compared against responseHash to authorise the payout.
String parameter _question of set_game(), written into the question state variable.
String parameter _response of set_game(), hashed into responseHash during initialisation.
String parameter _question of NewQuestion(), written into the question state variable.
bytes32 parameter _responseHash of NewQuestion(), written into responseHash.
Address parameter newAddress of newQuestioner(), stored into questionSender.

edges.reason: The _response parameter of Try() is hashed and compared with responseHash, controlling whether the balance transfer executes.
_response of set_game() is hashed with keccak256 and stored into responseHash.
_question of set_game() is written into the question state variable.
_question of NewQuestion() overwrites the question state variable.
_responseHash of NewQuestion() overwrites the responseHash state variable.
newAddress of newQuestioner() is stored into questionSender, transferring contract ownership.
In set_game() the caller msg.sender becomes questionSender while responseHash is unset, letting the first caller claim administrative ownership.
The full contract balance is transferred to the caller-controlled msg.sender, an external ETH send to an untrusted address.
tx.origin is read in require(msg.sender == tx.origin), gating the reward path on transaction origin rather than a trusted authorisation.
msg.sender is compared against tx.origin and used as the beneficiary of the payout inside Try().
Meeting the answer and msg.value > 3 ether conditions in Try() executes the external balance transfer to msg.sender.
Once require(msg.sender == questionSender) passes, StopGame() performs an external balance transfer to msg.sender.
StopGame() branches on require(msg.sender == questionSender), a caller-controlled access-control condition.
NewQuestion() branches on the caller-controlled comparison msg.sender == questionSender before rewriting state.
newQuestioner() branches on msg.sender == questionSender before handing over ownership.
questionSender is read as the authorisation reference for the msg.sender check in NewQuestion().
questionSender is read as the authorisation reference for the require(msg.sender == questionSender) in StopGame().
questionSender is read as the authorisation reference for the owner check in newQuestioner().
set_game() reads responseHash and only initialises the game while it is still 0x0.
The external transfer in Try() may re-enter the contract through the payable fallback function of the receiving address.
The external transfer in StopGame() may invoke the payable fallback function of the receiving address.

normalization_plan.reason: Local parameter of Try(); it only exists to hash-compare against responseHash and should be folded into the Try() function node.
Local parameter of set_game(); it is consumed immediately by the question state write and should be folded into set_game().
Local parameter of set_game(); it is hashed directly into responseHash and should be folded into set_game().
Local parameter of NewQuestion(); it only feeds the question state write and should be folded into NewQuestion().
Local parameter of NewQuestion(); it only feeds the responseHash write and should be folded into NewQuestion().
Local parameter of newQuestioner(); it is assigned to questionSender and should be folded into newQuestioner().
